speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with systemic hypertension; please tell me, how old are you and have you noticed any headaches, blurred vision, or chest pain lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; since he is a 5-year-old with no family history and was found to have hypertension, this suggests a secondary cause. Did he have any recent respiratory infections, fever, or urinary symptoms like pain or frequency? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Serum_Electrolytes, Renal_Function_Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Renovascular hypertension secondary to renal artery stenosis (likely fibromuscular dysplasia). The discrepancy in blood pressure between the right upper extremity and the rest of the body indicates a proximal obstruction; please order renal artery Doppler ultrasound and renal venous Doppler imaging immediately.
